title: Ethiopian Bean and Carrot Stew
community: All of Ethiopia — the string bean and carrot fasting combination
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Fasolia ke-Karot — string beans and carrots cooked together with onion, garlic, turmeric, and tomato. The vegetable pair that appears consistently on Ethiopian fasting platters — the green beans and orange carrots providing both nutritional balance and visual beauty.
longDesc: The combination of string beans and carrots is a classic Ethiopian fasting platter vegetable — the green and orange combination is as visually appealing as it is nutritionally complementary. The simple spicing lets the vegetables' natural flavours dominate.
ingredients: 3 medium carrots — sliced on the diagonal
steps: Heat oil. Cook onion until golden.
Add garlic, turmeric, and cumin. Stir 30 seconds.
Cook covered 10 more minutes until both are tender.
chefTips: Carrots before beans — they take longer.
Diagonal carrot slices cook faster than rounds.
cookingScience: Carrots' beta-carotene is fat-soluble — the oil in this dish dramatically increases the bioavailability of the beta-carotene compared to raw or water-cooked carrots. The cooking process ruptures the carrot's cell walls, releasing the beta-carotene into the oil.
sustainabilityTips: Both vegetables grown abundantly in Ethiopian highlands.
servedWith: As a vegetable side on non-fasting days
healthBenefits: Vitamins K and C from beans.
culturalNote: Fasolia ke-Karot provides the colour and nutrition of the fasting platter — its green and orange cheerfulness brightens the table alongside the reds and yellows of the lentil stews.
